rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both letters present the March 1954 foreign-economic-policy program, identify extension and amendment of the Trade Agreements legislation as its central unfinished component, anticipate congressional action early the following year, discuss renegotiating or developing GATT's organizational arrangements, and frame expanded trade and investment as essential to a stronger free world. C03 closely shares the policy framing but provides less of the child's detailed sequence. C04 supplies an earlier conceptual progression from postwar recovery and aid toward self-sustaining trade, but its language and immediate administrative purpose are less closely aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I recommended in March of this year a program for expanding international trade and overseas investment, for promoting currency convertibility, and for reducing the need for economic aid.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the foreign economic policy proposals contained in my Message to the Congress of March thirtieth... assistance... to nations which undertake convertibility of their currencies... encouragement to overseas investment
shared_material.explanation: Both summarize the same March program through the same cluster of trade, overseas investment, and currency-convertibility measures.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The remaining parts, especially the heart of the program--extension and amendment of our Trade Agreements Act--will... be pressed at the session of the Congress which begins in January
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the heart of the program--extension of and amendment of the Trade Agreements Extension Act of 1951... the prospect for consideration by the Congress early next year is excellent
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive 'heart of the program' formulation, the same legislative measure, and the same early-next-year timetable strongly indicate reused drafting material.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It would also seem essential that an effective organization be established for the administration of the Agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: renegotiation of the organizational provisions of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade for submission to the Congress
shared_material.explanation: Both treat revision of GATT's organizational or administrative machinery as a component of the program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The task before the contracting parties... is one of crucial significance to the further economic growth of the free world.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a minimum essential program for the building of a stronger America as an integral part of a strong and economically vigorous free world
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C13's framing of the program as indispensable to the economic vigor and strength of the free world.
